claims.text: Only the LiteLLM container holds the gateway keys, and only the api and LiteLLM containers publish ports, both on loopback.
Task containers reach the LiteLLM gateway over the homelab-tasks network and need a task token.
The runs service mounts the launcher socket /run/homelab-launcher.sock, and its client sends requests to that path; the launcher's caller list admits uid 21020, the uid runs runs as.
The launcher socket path is /run/homelab-launcher.sock.
A task's prepare step reaches the package indexes only through package-proxy on the homelab-packages network, over HTTPS.
The chat route uses Vercel AI Gateway.
The embed route uses llama-embed.
The embed-large route uses llama-embed-large.
The mac-router part serves vision.
The mac-router part serves embed-large-bulk.
The api part is the FastAPI app under src/homelab/api serving knowledge, run, decisions, image-cost, management and health endpoints on 127.0.0.1:8000.
The worker is a Procrastinate worker serving the local and default queues.
Postgres runs the pgvector image for Postgres 17 as a Compose service.
The gateway is LiteLLM with Home Lab's hooks, routed by config/litellm.yaml and published on 127.0.0.1:4000.
llama-embed serves Nemotron for embed and llama-embed-large serves Qwen3-Embedding-4B for embed-large, both on CPU.
package-proxy is a tinyproxy that allows HTTPS to the package indexes for a task's prepare step.
Knowledge ingestion and retrieval use LlamaIndex in src/homelab/knowledge, run from the api, the worker and the CLI.
The homelab command offers ingest, providers, routes and eval subcommands.
src/homelab/tasks holds the task, attempt and trace tables used with the submit, claim and finish commands.
runs is the execution service, a Compose service under the runs profile running as uid 21020.
The launcher is a socket-activated root helper that starts fixed fence and task container shapes.
The fence is a CLI image with an allow-list proxy.
The deployer is a root socket helper that installs application images.
homelab-task-runner.service runs homelab-task-runner, which consumes the tasks queue and runs each task through homelab-task-run.
The Telegram bot is a host service built on python-telegram-bot that runs as homelab-bot.
The data volumes are the encrypted main and bulk volumes with homelab-data.target.
homelab-notify.sh posts plain text to allowlisted Telegram chats for the watchdog and failure notifier.
homelab-dump.timer runs daily.
homelab-restore-check is the on-demand restore check.
homelab-copy streams the encrypted originals.
The code context server is an on-demand Serena MCP container with no network.
The Mac router is a native llama.cpp router that serves vision and embed-large-bulk.
homelab-profile provides profile switching, a model registry, calendar jobs and the job queue.
The Mac action listener listens on TCP 8091.
The menu bar app under mac/MenuBar is a Swift package that decodes homelab-profile's JSON.
Home Lab hooks add the task-network policy.
Home Lab hooks handle requests under /v1/videos.
Home Lab hooks set the x-homelab-cost-usd response header.
Home Lab hooks insert image charges into homelab_image_costs.
LlamaIndex packages provide the core, Postgres vector and document stores, and embedding and LLM clients.
Procrastinate apps provide the job machinery for the worker and for the runs service's queues.
The bot uses python-telegram-bot's Application, long polling and command registration.
llama.cpp owns local model loading on the node.
llama.cpp owns local model loading on the Mac.
The Mac router adds sleep-idle-seconds to its model preset.
The Mac router starts llama.cpp with --models-preset.
Clients send a purpose name as model to /v1 on the gateway.
The gateway logs one model_call audit line per call.
Clients learn purposes from GET /v1/models.
The answer endpoint embeds the question with embed, retrieves chunks and asks chat to answer only from the numbered chunks with citations.
POST /v1/runs checks the caller's run key, then one transaction writes the run and its task and defers the Procrastinate job.
The runs service claims jobs from the runs queue.
The launcher client connects to /run/homelab-launcher.sock.
The delivery code obtains a GitHub App token before pushing.
Clients read runs with GET /v1/runs and GET /v1/runs/{run_id}.
POST /v1/decisions calls the provider adapter, aggregates the repeats and refuses calls once the monthly budget is reached.
Image and video charges are added to homelab_image_costs, and GET /v1/images/cost reads the bearer key's total.
A periodic job every minute reads the Mac's offer and stores it in homelab_providers; homelab providers prints it.
homelab.service builds and starts the checked-out stack, and the deployer accepts a socket install only for an application named in its automatic list, which names factory.
Jobs persist before acknowledgement; the worker serves default (ping, provider offer) and local with concurrency 1 (ingest_brain).
run_coding_task is registered on the tasks queue and raises if the worker runs it; whole-run work uses the runs queue.
Postgres holds homelab_image_costs, homelab_video_jobs, homelab_decision_calls and homelab_providers alongside the task tables.
The API applies the image, video and decisions migrations at startup, and the worker applies Procrastinate's schema and the task schema before it starts.
The daily dump covers every non-template database in the cluster.
homelab.service runs the Compose stack after homelab-data.target and stops with it.
Mac tools run from a private installed copy under ~/Library/Application Support/homelab/mac.
The Mac router serves on its Tailscale address, port 8090.
Mac tools reach the node as the homelab-agent SSH account.
Gateway keys are Compose secrets, the bot token is a systemd encrypted credential, and the decisions provider key reaches only the api through its environment.
Only api and LiteLLM publish ports, on loopback; the bot's order listener binds the Tailscale IPv4 on TCP 8110 and ufw accepts 8110 from 172.18.0.0/16.
Brain is mounted read-only into the api and worker containers.
Postgres data and the models live under the LUKS-backed /srv/homelab and /srv/homelab-bulk mounts.
The api and worker (through the shared service defaults), LiteLLM, runs, llama-embed-large and package-proxy drop all capabilities and set no-new-privileges.
LiteLLM, runs and llama-embed-large set a non-root user, the platform image's last user is uid 10001, and package-proxy's image runs as node.
The postgres and llama-embed service definitions set neither cap_drop nor a user.
Logging prompts and retrieved text is off by default; ids, sizes and timings are logged.
Typed decisions refuse calls with 429 once the month's recorded cost reaches the configured cap.
Jobs are persisted before acknowledgement, and tasks are idempotent or declare retry=0.
Ingestion embeds with the local embed route, and the answer prompt contains only the question and the retrieved chunks.
vision goes to the Mac router and vision:xhigh to the hosted gateway model.
Run requests and messages carry contract 1.
run_contract.py defines the request shape, runs.py the routes, run_keys.py the scopes, and executors.yaml the catalogue.
Run keys have the fields application, sha256, scopes and repositories.
The decisions API is defined in decisions.py with the table in decisions.sql.
POST /v1/decisions requires a bearer run key whose scopes include decisions:write.
Purposes live in config/litellm.yaml, policy in litellm_hooks.py, and the homelab-models network in compose.yaml.
The Telegram bot and this repository's api use the gateway.
Media models are in media_model_list in config/litellm.yaml, video job metadata in video_jobs.py and image cost accounting in image_costs.py.
The gateway handles video routes and the api serves GET /v1/images/cost.
app.py defines KnowledgeQuery and the query and answer routes.
The bot's /ask posts the question as JSON to /v1/knowledge/answer, which the api serves.
The answer response has answer, refused and sources.
Clients are configured by HOMELAB_MODELS_BASE_URL and HOMELAB_MODELS_API_KEY.
The launcher socket unit listens on /run/homelab-launcher.sock, and the launcher reads one newline-terminated JSON line of at most 64 KiB per connection.
Callers 21010, 21011 and 21020 are permitted launcher profiles.
read_only, stdin and stream are optional launcher fields defaulting to false.
uid 21010 may only install through the deployer; uid 0 may install and roll back.
The deployer requires exactly the manifest's seven fields, and automatic lists factory.
change-classes lines are a class followed by a pattern.
The change-classes file is read by the runner before a merge and the deployer before an install.
Files under .github are class 4.
The order listener offers exactly GET /orders and POST /orders/<id>/ack on TCP 8110.
homelab-inbox accepts list, file and done.
homelab-queue-notice takes text on stdin, optionally with --task.
The Mac queue and the host runner call homelab-queue-notice.
offer.py writes public/homelab-offer.json, the router creates public/homelab-profile.json when it is absent, and providers.py reads the offer from the router's /homelab-offer.json.
The offer reader forbids unknown fields.
The listener runs on TCP 8091 and the bot posts to /backup with an empty body.
homelab-profile accepts profiles.json versions 1 and 2.
The menu app decodes a services map whose entries carry optional allowed, state and running fields.
The context server runs docker with stdin and no network.
Serena's configuration lists six fixed tools: find_symbol, get_symbols_overview, find_referencing_symbols, find_declaration, find_implementations and search_for_pattern.
Postgres 17 has the fixed address 172.18.0.2 on the default network.
homelab-dump dumps every non-template database.
Unlock opens main with the passphrase, opens bulk with a key file, then starts containerd, Docker and homelab-data.target.
Lock stops the target, Docker and its socket, and containerd, then unmounts and closes bulk before main.
The bulk key must be a root:root 0400 file of 4096 bytes.
Models default to /srv/homelab-bulk/models; Docker uses /srv/homelab-bulk/docker and containerd /srv/homelab-bulk/containerd.
The default Docker builder has GC enabled with a 50GB default keep storage.
homelab.service runs docker compose up -d --build from the checkout and does not pull.
LiteLLM mounts ./config read-only from the checkout.
Postgres has a fixed IPv4 address and every Compose network has a fixed subnet.
/health returns status ok, the version, the purposes and the models base URL.
Compose services use the journald log driver.
Startup schema statements create tables and columns only if they do not exist.
Development runs uv sync and uv run pytest, and pytest collects the tests directory.
The homelab CLI has routes and eval commands.
homelab-dump runs daily and dumps every non-template database.
Dumps are written with mode 0640, fsynced, and seven dated dumps are kept per database.
The restore check restores into a container with no network and prints ok on success.
For an install whose manifest has a migration, the deployer starts homelab-dump.service first and finishes the install as migration failed if the dump or the migration command fails.
The stack unit builds the checked-out code with compose up --build.
The managed crypttab and fstab entries register both volumes with noauto.
The docker.service, docker.socket and containerd.service drop-ins refuse to start unless /srv/homelab and /srv/homelab-bulk are both mount points.
ufw allows tailscale0 and 41641/udp on Wi-Fi, and DOCKER-USER drops inbound traffic from wlp1s0 and eno1.
Console shells set a read-only TMOUT of 900 seconds.
The bot, notifier and watchdog load token.cred as the bot-token credential, which is sealed to the TPM2 without PCR binding.
Both gateway key files are Compose secrets listed only on the LiteLLM service, whose entrypoint reads them at startup.
Unset Mac URLs default to a closed loopback endpoint.
Compose substitutes HOMELAB_DB_PASSWORD and the brain, corpus, Postgres and models paths, which .env.example lists for the .env file Compose reads.
llama-embed-large runs as 10001:10001 and downloads Qwen3-Embedding-4B Q8_0 into the models/embed-large directory.
The active collection defaults to about_aleix and can be brain.
The watchdog timer runs 90 seconds after boot.
HOMELAB_RUN_ROLES is passed to the api and runs services, defaults to empty and decides which run roles are enabled.
Only the api mounts /etc/homelab/run-keys.json read-only.
The bot replies with fixed texts for no card, a finished copy, a failed copy and an unreachable Mac.
The Mac copy refuses the startup volume and its APFS container and names files homelab-originals-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.tar.age.
homelab-copy lists every *-data/originals folder and the inbox when present, and streams one tar archive through age to the recipient file.
The last good copy is recorded in /var/lib/homelab-copy/last-good.json.
A daily persistent timer reminds through the notifier when the copy is more than seven days old or missing.
The api serves /v1/manage/routes and /v1/manage/providers.
Local provider checks call /models with a two-second timeout and cache the state for 30 seconds.
Management documents carry the SHA-256 of the route table file as their version.
homelab.service only runs docker compose against the checkout.
Host files record their installed path, for example homelab.service at /etc/systemd/system.
node/etc/crypttab and node/etc/fstab hold only the two managed homelab entries.
The credential drop-ins load the TPM2-sealed token.cred by its path under /etc/homelab-telegram-bot, not by contents.
The sudoers file is validated with visudo and installed with mode 0440, the file mode the installed-modes table gives for node/etc/sudoers.d.
The SSH hardening file is installed with mode 0600.
The ufw files are installed with mode 0640.
rules.d is root:polkitd 0750 and the rule 0644.
Scripts in /usr/local/sbin are installed 0755.
Units are installed 0644.
Bot Python files are installed 0644.
The link test checks the document map, relative links and anchors, and that cited paths exist and ranges lie inside the file.
CI syncs with the benchmark and telegram-bot groups, runs ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest, builds the image and builds the menu bar app.
CI also runs shellcheck, validates Docker and containerd configuration, checks bot requirements on Python 3.14, smoke-tests LiteLLM offline, runs gitleaks and builds the fence images.
config/litellm.yaml is the only route table.
homelab.service builds the images with compose up --build.
The project provides model access, knowledge retrieval and durable jobs, plus contained execution and Mac tools.
pytest collects tests/test_docs_links.py, which checks the map, links and anchors, and claims citations.

Factory's docs-verify calls the api's POST /v1/decisions with a bearer run key that holds decisions:write.
Factory's runner (uid 21010) calls the launcher socket for cli-run, bundle and usage.
Factory's sessions service (uid 21011) calls the launcher socket for chat, cli-run and bundle.
Factory's runner (uid 21010) asks the deployer to install Factory, which the factory.json manifest describes.
Factory collects queued orders from the bot's order endpoint on TCP 8110, over Tailscale or from the Compose default network.
med-ask calls the gateway over the homelab-models network.
The api reads and writes its tables in Postgres through HOMELAB_DATABASE_URL.
The worker's Procrastinate app connects to Postgres through HOMELAB_DATABASE_URL and stores jobs there.
The api calls purposes on the gateway at HOMELAB_MODELS_BASE_URL.
The worker's ingest job embeds through the gateway's embed purpose.
The homelab CLI lists purposes from the gateway's /models endpoint and embeds through the gateway.
The gateway routes embed and embed-large to the llama-embed and llama-embed-large llama.cpp servers.
The gateway sends vision and embed-large-bulk calls to the Mac router's URL taken from the private environment.
The gateway's hooks add image charges to homelab_image_costs.
The worker reads the Mac's homelab-offer.json that the profile tools publish through the router.
The api's query and answer endpoints use the knowledge module's retrieval.
The knowledge module stores vectors and documents in Postgres.
The api's run routes create runs through the task store.
runs claims whole-run jobs from the task store's Procrastinate queue.
The task store's tables live in Postgres.
runs (uid 21020) asks the launcher socket for task and CLI containers.
runs writes task token files that the gateway reads from its read-only token mount.
The launcher imports homelab-fence's builders, uses its homelab-fence network for the fence profiles, and the fence's own compose file defines that network.
The prepare shape uses the homelab-packages network and package-proxy as HTTPS_PROXY.
The host runner sends failure notices through homelab-queue-notice.
The host runner claims through the task store's claim command in the worker container.
The deployer runs homelab-dump.service before a migration.
After a failed install the deployer starts homelab-notify@deployer.service, and the notifier maps the deployer alias to homelab-deployer.service.
The image cost notice runs the api's image_costs alerts command through docker compose exec and sends each message through homelab-notify.sh.
The bot's /ask posts to the api's loopback answer endpoint.
The bot asks the frontline purpose on the gateway's loopback port.
The bot's /backup posts once to the Mac listener's /backup.
The listener runs the Mac copy command, which streams homelab-copy over SSH.
The Mac queue sends notices with ssh homelab-agent sudo -n homelab-queue-notice.
homelab-profile writes the router's presets, then reloads and loads native models through the router's API.
The menu bar app runs the homelab-profile command recorded in its bundle and decodes its JSON.
The embedding servers keep models under the bulk volume's models directory.
Postgres data lives on the main encrypted volume.
The context server refuses to run while the data volume is locked.
homelab-dump dumps every non-template database in the Postgres container.
The bot keeps its planning data under /srv/homelab/frontline on the main volume, and the originals copy reads the bot inbox from frontline/inbox.
